title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues Grothendieck's analysis of a set of triples (alpha, beta, mu). Here alpha lies in an extended profinite group G' = G ⋊ {1, tau'}, beta in G, and mu in Ẑ^×. The triples are classified by invariants (xi, eta, mu) = ([alpha, rho], eps_2(mu)[beta, sigma], mu), the map (49) of the previous page.

Setting. rho and sigma are torsion elements of G (very plausibly the images of the order-3 and order-2 generators of a profinite (P)SL_2(Z)-type group). tau' is an involution of 'complex-conjugation' type (it inverts rho and sigma up to conjugacy). Z_rho, Z_sigma are centralizers and N_rho, N_sigma are normalizers of the cyclic groups generated by rho and sigma. nu_2(mu) and nu_3(mu) are exponents with eps_i(mu) = (-1)^{nu_i(mu)}. B_{rho,sigma} is the group of u carrying the 'base' data; the previous page gives a section (52), u -> (u, u tau^{nu_2(mu)}, chi_B(u)).

(53): the fibre of (49) over the invariants of u is the coset G_{rho,sigma}(u, mu) = {(u a_0^{-1}, u tau'^{nu_2} b_0^{-1}, mu) : a_0 in Z_rho, b_0 in Z_sigma}. Equivalently, after setting b = b_0 tau'^{nu_2}, it is {(u a_0^{-1}, u b^{-1}, mu)}. So each fibre is a torsor under Z_rho × Z_sigma.

(54)-(55): this is rewritten using the exact sequence 1 -> Z_sigma -> N_sigma --eps_sigma--> {±1} = {1, tau'} -> 1. In this form b ranges over N_sigma subject to eps_sigma(b) = eps_2(mu).

(56)-(57): restricting to the 'special' part SG^eff, i.e. requiring alpha tau'^{nu_3} and beta to lie in the subgroup 𝔊 = ker delta_G, gives a common condition: delta_G(u) = delta_sigma(b) = delta_rho(tau'^{nu_3} a_0).

With a = tau'^{nu_3} a_0 in N_rho, the fibre becomes {(u a^{-1} tau'^{nu_3}, u b^{-1}, mu) : a in N_rho, b in N_sigma, eps_rho(a) = eps_3(mu), eps_sigma(b) = eps_2(mu), delta_rho(a) = delta_sigma(b) = delta_G(u)}.

This motivates the group M_{rho,sigma}[0] = B_{rho,sigma} ×_{T} N_rho ×_{T} N_sigma, a fibre product over the abelian target T_{rho,sigma} of the delta maps. It comes with the composite characters eps_rho, eps_sigma: M -> {±1}.

On the next page the 'effective' subgroup M^eff is cut out as the coincidence subgroup of (eps_sigma, eps_rho) and (eps_2, eps_3)∘chi. It is shown to be in bijection with SG^eff via (u, a, b) -> (u a^{-1} tau'^{nu(a)}, u b^{-1}, chi(u)).

Purpose: to endow the a priori mere set of solutions of the 'loop equation' (automorphism-type data of a profinite modular/braid group with cyclotomic character mu) with a group structure. It becomes an explicit fibre product of normalizers of the torsion elements. This is Grothendieck's route towards a Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group.
errors: Sign/convention inconsistency: in (54) beta is written u·i_sigma(b), while in (53) and in the final formula it is u·b^{-1}. With beta = u·i_sigma(b), the condition delta_G(beta) = 1 gives delta_G(u) = delta_sigma(b)^{-1}, not delta_sigma(b) as in (57). It is harmless after replacing b by b^{-1}, which is consistent with the later formula.
Equation numbers (54), (55), (56) are reused twice on the page (an editing slip).
The final displayed set is labelled G_{rho,sigma}(u, mu), but it already includes the delta-conditions, so it is really the fibre of SG^eff (the 'S' is missing).
B_{rho,sigma} is crossed out in the definition of M_{rho,sigma}[0], yet it is used as the first factor on the next page. The next page also writes b in Z_sigma where N_sigma is meant.

Otherwise the algebra checks out. a = tau'^{nu_3} a_0 gives a^{-1} tau'^{nu_3} = a_0^{-1}, so alpha is unchanged. a_0 in Z_rho iff eps_rho(a) = (-1)^{nu_3} = eps_3(mu). The delta-identities are consistent because delta(tau')^2 = 1.

ideas.what: Fibres of the commutator-invariant map (alpha, beta, mu) -> ([alpha, rho], [beta, sigma], mu) are cosets (torsors) under centralizers Z_rho × Z_sigma.
ideas.modern_name: Torsor description of conjugating elements / centralizer cosets

ideas.what: Replacing centralizer conditions by normalizer conditions via the exact sequence 1 -> Z_sigma -> N_sigma -> {±1} -> 1, with the sign tied to the cyclotomic parity eps_i(mu).
ideas.modern_name: Normalizers of finite cyclic subgroups in profinite (P)SL_2(Z)/(P)GL_2(Z); sign/inversion character
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard; normalizers of torsion in profinite free products studied by Herfort–Ribes and others

ideas.what: Packaging the solution set as an explicit group: a fibre product M = B ×_T N_rho ×_T N_sigma over an abelian group T, then cutting out an 'effective' coincidence subgroup that bijects onto SG^eff.
ideas.modern_name: Group-theoretic model of a GT-type solution set (fibre product of normalizers over an abelianization-type target)
ideas.usually_credited_to: GT-type groups via Drinfeld (1990), Ihara, Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura–Schneps; this specific fibre-product model is not attested

missed.claim: Grothendieck builds a fibre-product group M_{rho,sigma}[0] = B ×_T N_rho ×_T N_sigma from normalizers of the order-2 and order-3 torsion elements, together with sign characters. Its effective coincidence subgroup is meant to parametrize the 'special effective' solutions of his loop equation group-theoretically. This is a concrete, possibly computable model of a GT-like group via normalizers in profinite modular groups, and it does not seem to be used in the literature.
missed.quote: Introduisons donc le groupe M_{ρ,σ}[0] = B_{ρ,σ} ×_{δ_{ρ,σ}} N_ρ ×_{δ_{ρ,σ}} N_σ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could give an alternative description of GT-hat-type groups (or variants such as those of Nakamura–Schneps and Minamide–Nakamura) in terms of centralizers and normalizers in profinite PSL_2(Z)/PGL_2(Z). That might clarify the 'complex conjugation' (tau') parity conditions. The value is modest and depends on the surrounding pages.

deep.surprise_reason: These are technical, essentially routine group-theoretic manipulations within an unpublished programme. The fibre-product packaging is a mildly original organizational device, but it is not a striking result in itself.
transcription_corrections: Header '53 [?]' is likely the page tag '57δ' or similar, written above the first line.
In (56) the crossed-out symbol before '= u a_0^{-1} τ'^{ν_3(μ)}' is α, and the target group is the special subgroup 𝔊 (ker δ_G).
On the second line of (56), 'δ_G(u i_σ(b)) = 1' is correct.
The final formula is numbered (54) again on the page (it should be 58). The subsequent (55) and (56) are likewise duplicate numbers.
The note next to (56) reads roughly 'notés ε'_ρ' with the next line '(encore notés ε_ρ, ε_σ par abus de notation)'.
